diagnosis.narrative: The series is dominated by a strong upward trend (a net rise of ~137% of its level). There is little seasonal structure. The series is quite predictable: its energy concentrates in a few structured frequencies. The series reads as non-stationary by the ADF/KPSS tests. A few outliers stand out (29 points, ~7% of the sample). Across validation windows the model ranking is unstable (Kendall tau 0.072), which favours a robust combination.

But weights must be method or handle; inverse_error is method. That would be new. Let's do evaluate_strategy combine weighted, models pool5, weights inverse_error.

Test a robust weighted combination using dba on the moderately stable pool2 to see if it beats the trimmed mean pool1 leader.
Test a robust dba combination on the larger pool4 to see if it improves over trimmed_mean pool1.
Test a weighted combination using inverse error on a larger stable pool to see if it improves over mean and trimmed_mean.
Test a robust median combination on a larger, more diverse pool (pool4) to see if it improves over trimmed_mean pool1.
Test a weighted combination on pool5 using inverse_error weights to see if adding more diverse models helps over trimmed_mean pool1.

decision.justification: Selected 'trimmed_mean on pool1' (a seeded deterministic baseline) as the best of 22 backtested attempts, score 0.5589. Series context: trend strength 0.9136 and seasonal strength 0.1717; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau 0.072); 4 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 0.387.
